codeReview.summary: The fix correctly replaces executeWorkstream() with loadModelConfig() + callModel() in src/integrate/cli.ts, resolving all three original blocking issues. (1) parseModelResponse (which expects ## CHANGES format) is no longer called; the raw AI response goes directly to parseTestFilesFromAIResponse which correctly handles plain JSON arrays of test files. (2) applyChanges (which writes files to disk with the wrong format) is no longer called since executeWorkstream is not invoked; runIntegrationTests handles file writing exclusively. (3) The format mismatch is resolved because parseTestFilesFromAIResponse expects {path, content, language, framework, testCount} objects matching the integration prompt, no longer going through {file, action, content} format. The diff is minimal and surgical: only the import line, the Step 5 code block, and the corresponding test assertion comments were changed. All verification commands pass (typecheck, build, 14 CLI tests, CLI --help, NO_EXECUTE_ARTIFACT error).

issues.description: The structural assertion test 'runIntegrateCommand reuses loadModelConfig and callModel from model-connector' only checks that runIntegrateCommand and parseTestFilesFromAIResponse are functions — it does not verify that loadModelConfig or callModel are actually imported or reachable from the cli module. The comment claims 'the typechecker confirms loadModelConfig and callModel come from the model-connector module,' which is true (import errors would fail typecheck), but runtime reflection could verify this more robustly (e.g., checking that the module re-exports loadModelConfig). This is a pre-existing weakness from the original test, not a regression.
Pre-existing: The --force CLI option is accepted but never checked or implemented in runIntegrateCommand. It is a no-op flag. Not introduced by this fix.
Pre-existing: Missing tests for NO_TEST_FILES_GENERATED, TEST_RUN_FAILED, and IO_ERROR error codes. The success path (exitCode=0) is also untested. Not introduced by this fix.
